summary: Specializing in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies, the 13th Dalai Lama studied under Agvan Dorzhiev, Pa Ri Rabsal, Tertön Sogyal, and others. He taught numerous prominent figures, including Rangjung Rigpe Dorje and the 9th Panchen Lama.

Working in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology, he studied under mentors including Trijang Rinpoche, Ling Rinpoche, and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche. He founded the International Network of Engaged Buddhists (1989) and the Mind and Life Institute (1990).

A scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, he studied under Kalu Rinpoche, Beru Khyentse Rinpoche I, and Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche. Over his career, he taught many students, including Reginald A. Ray and Chökyi Nyima Rinpoche.
Active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, he studied under Jamphel Yeshe Gyaltsen from circa 1930 to 1940, as well as under Ngawang Lobzang Gyatso and Khangsar Dorje Chang.

id: P:3rd Sras Rinpoche Thubten Kalsang Bstanpai Gyaltsen
summary: A Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar, he studied under the 96th Ganden Tripa Thubten Kunga and at Drepung Loseling Monastery and Gyume Tantric College. He held posts at Drepung Loseling, Gyume Tantric College, and Rizong Monastery.

Specializing in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, he studied at Drepung Monastery (~1951–1959). He held positions at the Central School for Tibetans (1960, 1965–1970) and served as head of the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (1971–2001).
A Drö Khenpo Yeshe Gyatso studied under Shenphen Nangwa and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.
A Dzom Gyalsé Gyurmé Dorjé studied under Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang and Ayu Khandro, and later taught Nyoshul Khenpo Rinpoche.
After studying at Pachaiyappa's College (~1907–1911), he held a post there from 1911 to 1918. He subsequently served as a professor at the University of Mysore from 1918 to 1947.
Working in Indology and philosophy, he served as a Pandit at the Karnataka State Archaeology Department and was attested as head of Yatiraja Mutt in 1926.
An Indology scholar, he served as Senior Dakshina Fellow at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute and as Lecturer on Sanskrit at Karnatak Arts College, Dharwad.

Focusing on Buddhist studies, sinology, and japanology, Muller earned his PhD at Stony Brook under Sung-Bae Park. He held appointments at Toyo Gakuen University, the University of Tokyo, and became director of Musashino University's Buddhist culture institute in 2019.
Active in Indology and religious studies, he studied under Tirumalai Krishnamacharya from circa 1971 to 1989. In 1976, he founded the Krishnamacharya Yoga Mandiram.

A philosopher educated at Jesus College, Cambridge, he held posts at Swansea, University of Malta, Beaumont College, and Cardiff. He served as Gladstone Professor of Greek at the University of Liverpool (1950–1972) and founded Dionysius in 1977.

Specializing in philosophy and history/archaeology, Sabra studied at Alexandria University, London School of Economics, and under Karl Popper. He held academic posts at the Warburg Institute (1962–1972) and Harvard University (1972–1996).

Working in Indology and linguistics, he studied at Mysore and Indiana University Bloomington. He taught at MS University of Baroda and Deccan College before a long career at the University of Chicago (1962–1993), also visiting Harvard.
Active in Tibetology, A. M. D'Rozario completed an M.Sc. at the University of Allahabad and a Ph.D. at the University of Cambridge.
Working in Indology and philosophy, he served as Curator at the Oriental Research Institute Mysore (~1891–1916) and subsequently as Director of the Adyar Library and Research Centre (~1916–1926).

An Indologist who studied under K. V. Rangaswami Aiyangar, he served as joint editor for Brahmavidya at the Adyar Library and Research Centre (attested 1940–1950) and as librarian at the National Archives of India (attested 1954).

Active in linguistics and Indology, he completed his PhD under Ralph Lilley Turner at SOAS (~1930–1933). He held appointments at the University of Mysore, including as librarian and part-time professor of philology at Maharaja's College, Mysore.
